narrative: OMX30 faces conflicting signals on Monday open. While the index remains in bull regime (+5.8% above 200-MA) with strong ADX 59.1, technical overbought conditions (RSI 73.16, Stochastic K=88.8) pose mean-reversion risk. Global equity weakness—particularly NASDAQ -0.91% and Nikkei -2.42%—combined with VIX spike (+6.94%) and AI IPO underperformance creates headwind. The weighted correlation signal of -0.204% and US yield compression (-33bp to 5.137%) favor defensive rotation. USD/SEK strength (+0.41%) supports exporters, but Brent weakness (-1.73%) pressures industrial input costs, limiting upside. At 100% of 52-week range, the index is priced for perfection.
morningBrief: OMX30 opens to mixed signals in a risk-off Monday shaped by US tech selloff and Asia weakness. The index is overbought (RSI 73.16, Stochastic 88.8/90.5) despite bull regime—classic mean-reversion setup. Watch resistance at 3180 (50-MA); support sits 3085 (lower Bollinger band). USD/SEK +0.41% benefits exporters (Volvo, Atlas Copco, Ericsson), but oil -1.73% and broader sentiment deterioration offset gains. Defensive sectors (Banks via rate outlook, Pharma/Essity via risk-off rotation) outperform. VIX +6.94% suggests elevated volatility—expect choppy opens. Trade war diplomacy headlines (Yalta 2.0 reference) are tail risk. US Jobless Claims 14:30 CET could trigger midday repricing.
